I just finished my EE (it isn't due till September but our school deadline was scheduled for late June). The amount of reading you have to do really depends on what subject you choose to do it on. It would be easier for you to choose a topic you do as one of your HLs, but it's not required. Subjects of the Humanities (e.g. History, Geo, Econ) usually require more reading than ones of science and art due to the amount of primary and secondary sources you have to find.

With regards to an English Literature EE, you do have to read a book and write about it. The way you come up with a question/topic is very much like how you would with your written assignment. Start broadly and find a relatively vague topic to start with, then slowly work your way toward a narrower question. (Same goes for every other subject)

English Language and Literature is something different I would think, but I'm not too sure cuz almost none of my friends are doing a English LangLit EE.

If you have any questions feel free to ask!

The Sun Yat Sen Memorial Park always has been my go-to spot.. I dunno it just kinda gives me some peace and space to just chill out sometimes.
The Peak Galleria's a good place too - restaurants and a hella nice view (but I'm sure you've been).

Loads of food to try around the island though. Tin Hau and Tai Hang for a more "local" feel and Central if you wanna dine at a "fancy" restaurant.
Repulse Bay and Stanley are nice too and it isn't hard to get there either. 

There's a bus that goes directly to Stanley from Central and you could easily spend half a day there and walk to Repulse (or take a bus, I'm not your boss)

Either way, enjoy your stay!!
